name: A structural commit is observed only as one atomic safepoint publication

input.fixture_ref: Continuously observe two Classes from participating runtime threads while one transaction group changes both and publishes state and invalidation metadata.

applicability.reason: Held, with the blocker RE-MEASURED rather than carried forward. The earlier reason was that runtime values were not `Send`; that is now fixed (values are `Arc<Mutex<..>>` and cross a thread boundary, and `SourceEvaluator` is `Send`), so it is no longer what blocks this row. The remaining gap is narrower and was measured: META-C038 forms a transaction group through NESTED OPEN CALLS, but no source-level surface opens a group spanning two Classes. GRAMMAR `class_decl` makes `open` a declaration prefix, not a nestable block, and there is no `Reflection::Class.open`/transaction API. Each declaration therefore publishes its OWN group: two Classes declared in one load were measured at commit_id 112 and 114, and two separate opens at 115 and 116. The observation surface this row needs already exists - `Reflection::Class.revision` reports `number` and `commit_id`, and C018 gives one group ONE shared commit_id, so a shared commit_id is exactly the 'never a partial structural mix' evidence. What is missing is the ability to PUT two Classes in one group from source. `ClassRegistry::commit_group`/`publish_all` already implement it internally, so this is an unexposed surface rather than an unimplemented mechanism.

expect.status: Observers see either both old revisions or both new revisions, never a partial structural mix, and execution resumes after atomic publication.
